conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Hey, I’m just trying to get through the day, you know? Sometimes little things remind me of past events, like when I heard a sudden loud noise outside, and it just hit me hard, like I was right back there again. It's exhausting.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds really tough. When that loud noise happened, what kind of feelings or thoughts did it bring up for you in that moment?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: When that noise happened, my heart just started racing, and I felt this wave of panic wash over me. It was like all those awful memories rushed back, and I couldn’t catch my breath for a moment. It made me feel so overwhelmed, like I was back in that place, and I just wanted to hide away from everything.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: It sounds like that experience was very intense. After feeling that wave of panic, what did you do next?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: After that wave of panic hit, I kind of froze for a bit, just stuck in my thoughts. I ended up sitting on the couch, trying to distract myself by scrolling through my phone, but my mind was still racing. It’s like I wanted to escape, but nothing really helped.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Sitting on the couch sounds like a way to try to find some comfort. While you were scrolling through your phone, what thoughts kept coming up for you?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: While I was scrolling, my mind kept drifting back to memories I wish I could forget. I kept thinking about how unfair everything felt, like I was stuck in this never-ending cycle. It felt really lonely, and I couldn't shake this feeling that I was the only one dealing with it.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That loneliness can be really challenging to cope with. Did you notice any specific physical sensations or changes in your body while you were having those thoughts?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yeah, I definitely felt my chest tightening, like I was being squeezed from the inside. My hands were kind of trembling, and I could feel this heaviness in my stomach, making it hard to think clearly. It was like my body was reflecting everything my mind was racing through.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: That sounds very uncomfortable. After experiencing those physical sensations, did anything help you feel even a little bit more at ease?
